title: What Counts as One Backtest?

launchpad.outcome: Tell a real rep from screenshots, candles and imagined setups, then log one rep with its screenshots attached.

slides.kicker: ONE REP = ONE INDEPENDENTLY EVALUATED OPPORTUNITY
slides.title: Rep or not?

items.text: A setup formed in replay. You evaluated it and took it. Logged with its decision and outcome.
Three screenshots of that same trade: before, entry, after.
items.why: Screenshots belong to the rep. They aren’t reps themselves.

items.text: Every candle you stepped through in the session.
A setup you think would have formed if price had pulled back a little more.
A setup formed. Your rules said no. You passed and logged the pass.
items.why: A pass on a real, evaluated opportunity is a rep.

items.text: Re-running a session you’ve already seen the result of.
items.why: You know the ending. That’s review, not a clean rep.

slides.title: Log one rep
lines: Run one opportunity. When you save it, notice: one rep, three screenshots attached to it.
slides.principle: A REP ONLY HELPS IF YOU KNOW EXACTLY WHAT YOU’RE REPEATING.

takeaways: One rep = one independently evaluated opportunity.
remember: A rep only helps if you know exactly what you’re repeating.
